method: Assistant-executed public-source research and self-review; not an automated or blinded test.
sampling: All three earlier picks plus first two awardees in saved NJEDA list, frozen before new searches.
interpretation: The initial two-organization screen finds credible leads but does not adequately distinguish accelerator recognition from deeper outside commitment. Comparative prioritization is a post-test reviewer judgment, not a pre-registered ranking metric.

companies.why: University license plus confirmed industrial development relationship, recognition and recent NJ program selection.
limits: Shared financing release counts once; partner publication is confirmation, not independent journalism.
Exact NJ municipality varies across sources.

companies.why: HAX profile and 2026 showcase, federal program recognition, documented industry conference appearance, and NJ presence.
limits: HAX and SOSV belong to the same source family.
Tulane work is proposed in an award abstract, not demonstrated as completed.
Trade interview is founder-supplied commentary, not independent product validation.
Earlier NY listing does not override newer specific NJ operating evidence.

companies.why: NETL confirms actual research collaboration; newer NJ program recognition and a federal portfolio strengthen identity and institutional links.
limits: NETL relationship report is August 2024; current agreement status is unverified.
NASA award records establish research-program participation, not endorsement or mission deployment.
Federal portfolio supports Energy/Materials alias association; formal legal continuity was not independently audited.

companies.why: Cleantech Open confirms 2025 accelerator participation; NJEDA documents 2026 program selection and NJ location.
limits: Passes the initial screen but has thinner evidence of substantial outside collaboration.
Rutgers event attendance is not a university partnership or license.
CSIT profile describes Rutgers-origin research; license and institutional relationship not independently confirmed.

companies.sector: AI for life sciences / regulatory software
companies.why: Real NJIT involvement and accelerator acceptance, but a new source lists New York headquarters.
limits: NJ ecosystem activity is supported; headquarters and extent of NJ company operations need clarification.
A directory is not a definitive headquarters authority, so do not label the company conclusively out of state.
Institutional program activity does not establish market adoption.
